work.name: School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
work.summary: I develop and apply multiscale simulation and machine-learning methods to understand reaction mechanisms at electrochemical interfaces and to design catalysts and energy materials, working with Prof. Li Shuzhou.
highlights: Electrocatalysis under realistic conditions: combined grand-canonical DFT and kinetic Monte Carlo to show that the active site of single-atom catalysts adapts dynamically during electrochemical reactions (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024).

Electrode/electrolyte interfaces: use ab initio molecular dynamics and machine-learning potentials to study how potential-dependent water structure and cations affect reactant transport, reaction kinetics and catalyst stability.
Energy storage: use first-principles simulations to understand the reaction mechanisms and interfacial chemistry behind battery performance and degradation (Energy Storage Materials 2026).

ML potentials for alloys: co-lead (corresponding author) of collaborative work with the University of Wollongong on active-learning ML interatomic potentials for refractory high-entropy alloys (J. Mater. Sci. Technol. 2025, Materials & Design 2024).
AI-driven research: building LLM-based research agents that run the hypothesis → simulation → analysis loop on HPC on their own.
Grant writing: drafted and submitted a research proposal on behalf of my supervisor (PI), which was awarded about S$1 million in funding from the Singapore Ministry of Education (MOE).
Collaborate closely with experimental groups to connect computed mechanisms with measured performance.

work.name: Faculty of Engineering and Information Sciences, University of Wollongong, Australia
work.summary: Co-lead the computational side of a collaboration with A/Prof. Hongtao Zhu on refractory high- and medium-entropy alloys for nuclear and high-temperature applications.
highlights: ML interatomic potentials: developed active-learning Deep Potential models to study chemical short-range order, mechanical strength and radiation damage in FeCrV- and CrTaTiMo-based alloys (J. Mater. Sci. Technol. 2025).
Oxidation and corrosion: used DFT and AIMD to reveal oxidation mechanisms in these alloys (Materials & Design 2024, Langmuir 2025, Corrosion Science 2025).

Irradiation resistance: combined first-principles calculations with experiments to explain how W doping and vacancies affect irradiation resistance and mechanical properties (J. Alloys Compd. 2023, Comput. Mater. Sci. 2025).
Corresponding author on joint papers, and co-supervise PhD students' computational work.

work.name: Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Bologna, Italy
work.summary: Worked with Prof. M. C. Righi on first-principles modeling of tribochemistry and superlubricity in carbon-based materials.
highlights: Surface chemistry of diamond: designed and ran DFT and AIMD simulations to reveal how H₂, H₂O and O₂ react with and passivate diamond surfaces, which controls adhesion and friction (Carbon 2022).
Wear and friction mechanisms: studied atomistic wear in diamond and the lubrication mechanism of oxidized diamond/silica interfaces (Langmuir 2023, ACS Appl. Nano Mater. 2023).
Green lubrication: contributed simulations to a collaboration with École Centrale de Lyon showing superlubricity from naturally derived aromatic molecules (Carbon 2024).
Wrote scientific papers and mentored undergraduate students.
